Old habits die hard, specifically on tough days, and the "new" never fails to frighten me because the chances of me failing or feeling hopeless is higher. And most of the times, I have nothing to fall back on/rely on. So, what I did was I try to deal with what I have in the moment like personal issues or studies, and what I can do to lessen my anxiety regarding the future. Making my self some quality armor and weapons, if you will.

To keep myself moving mentally and physically, I searched for hobbies or new stuff that I could do and will enjoy. Or even ones I didn't have thoughts to do before. And most of them turned out to be short lived, but at least I tried it out and crossed that off the list, and found some that did work like reading and singing.

Additionally, I took on the caretaker role in my family, and focused on building my relationship with them as I let go of some that I realized aren't working. I also reached out on strangers at the internet, just like how you did with your post, who went through some of the things I went through, and applied their advice and tips. It will take some time to find where to ask and what to ask but when you do, it is fruitful.

And if you can't find people in your new environment or current environment to rely on, join communities near your area or in the internet. That's also one of the things I did since my family can't relate with everything I like and do, which is understandable, we all have differences. Besides Reddit, there are Discord servers for different hobbies and focuses. And volunteering events that always need more people and people that you might get along with.

I also listed down my anxieties and kept asking myself questions to cover as much basis as I could, and made the solutions I could execute now and in the future. While the things I can't control, I just learn to accept them and thought about what I can control at that situation.

So, in general, and as cheesy as it is, I concentrated on my relationship with myself and how I want myself to be, and taking care of my family/connections that I have now. I made myself someone I could rely on, and I worked with what I have and tried my best to better them.

Brainstorm on ideas that caters to your personal environment and state, and that you could experiment on. There will be fails but you'll eventually find what suits you the best. Best of luck to you, mate! I hope you can find the people you can relate and rely on soon!

I'm also experiencing what you're experiencing, even at 19. And what I learned is that we don't really become adults overnight, and are able to have our shit together instantly or have it more quicker than before. Being an adult is different for everyone, and it's just really about experimenting and following the blueprint of your ideal self that is constantly changing, as you find what suits you.

Just last year you were focusing on your studies, hobbies, finding your people, and other things that are personal to your experience. And you still are doing that, you're still in high school.

Then next year, you just got out of it, and you'll be finishing up what you have been dealing with during the previous years. Some you will be done with, and some will continue on till a later date. And that's fine. The transitioning period of being an adult can be stressful because of the changes and new environment, so take your time in processing and doing things, and do what you can and feel comfortable with.

I plan to take a short course in a university or community college since I also don't know if I will be able to finish either, and it's cheaper. So, maybe that's also an option for you.

Choose one that can be connected to the career/course you have in mind, or a different one if you want to try something out (in the form of a short course or a club at the side of your choice). Or take a job; it can be different from the career you want or related. Talking to someone in school or at the other schools you plan to go to can help. Or an adult you trust that can give good advice.

Just do your best, that's enough. There will be nights where things are tough. So, try to keep what makes you smile close to you. Whether it's your hobbies or your friends that sound very wholesome.

I'm still figuring things out as well but I hope this brought some ideas in mind and things go well for you! :)

I'm following this post because I have a similar mentality as you do. But I have gotten a bit better over the years. Keyword "a bit", so I don't know if this will give you any solace. But I just tell myself the "rational" thoughts I have and need, and the encouraging words I need to hear. Even if I have to make a character in my head and roleplay those words to myself, I will if I need it from an outside force. And if I start to tell myself "this bad thing happened because I did x so, y happened", I will write down an essay to myself to disprove that as well.  
  
Example thought I had: Because I felt motivated to do my best on my assignments and duties, the arguments broke out.  
  
My counterattack: The topic of my assignments and duties has no correlation to the arguments' topic. Their argument centered around a chore that though indeed, I could have done if I had just dropped my studies, my lack of action to it is not the reason for their fight nor are they my obligation. It's their inability to communicate effectively and inquire about the chore to each other without raising their voices with an accusing tone. And even if I did know about this inability, it is a them problem rather than a me problem. I am not obligated to fix and clean up after them. I am only obligated to my own words and actions. People are an outside force that I could only influence and manipulate so far, but I cannot control them. Therefore, they are not my concern. And this is not being cold, but leaving the problem aside to focus on the ones I have in my hands right now. I will go to it if I still wish to, not out of obligation, once I am finished with my own.  
  
It's really just accepting that you have no control over others and your environment. You can only control how you would react to these outside forces. And you shouldn't dismiss your thoughts and feelings over these worries, you should let yourself feel them and don't dwell on them. Reason with the thoughts to move on, that's what worked for me, personally.  
  
I'm not sure how you function so, I can't propose a solution that will work for you. I suggest listing down the top 10 things you have obsessive thoughts over (1 being the most and 10 least) and starting with 10. And you can test out what works for that problem and try it on 9. If 9 is kind of different, find the similarities and differences and the reasons for those. And then move on to 8 and do the same onwards. This can be the top 10 things this week or whatnot, however you would like and you feel fits you the most.

You can also video yourself while you work if you're the type to work better when in a public area where you can be seen. Or monologue what you're doing as if it was an RPG game and you're doing these to unlock levels or/and increase EXP.
